articles.title: Pakistan steps up airport screening amid Ebola outbreak in Africa - Pakistan - DAWN.COM
articles.rephrased_article: Pakistan's health ministry has intensified airport screening measures and directed all provinces to remain on alert following the recent Ebola outbreak in Africa. The National Institutes of Health (NIH) and World Health Organisation’s (WHO) offices in Pakistan are monitoring the situation, while the ministry emphasized that the risk to Pakistan is extremely low due to limited travel links with affected countries.  The ministry also confirmed that it possesses the capacity to diagnose Ebola and has issued directives for preparedness measures.

articles.title: Iran war day 85: Tehran says major gaps remain in US talks | US-Israel war on Iran News | Al Jazeera
articles.rephrased_article: Pakistan’s army chief, Field Marshal Asim Munir, arrived in Tehran to intensify diplomatic efforts for a US-Iran peace deal. Iranian officials acknowledged significant gaps remain between the two sides despite ongoing talks and emphasized that ending the war is essential for any future agreement.  While Qatar has been praised for supporting Pakistani-led mediation efforts, tensions remain over Iran’s enriched uranium program and control of the Strait of Hormuz. The US continues to engage in diplomatic efforts with Iran, but major differences persist. Meanwhile, escalating violence between Israel and Lebanon has resulted in casualties and strained the Lebanese economy.

articles.title: Israel’s October 7 tribunal: Show trial of Palestinians or justice? | Israel-Palestine conflict News | Al Jazeera
articles.rephrased_article: Israel approved a special military tribunal to try Palestinians accused of participating in the October 7, 2023, Hamas-led attack.  The tribunal will have the power to impose the death penalty and has drawn criticism from international organizations including the United Nations, which called for its repeal. Human rights groups like Amnesty International and B'tselem condemn the legislation as a way of seeking revenge on imprisoned Palestinians, while some Israeli parliamentarians believe it will bring justice. The tribunal is expected to hold televised trials of an estimated 300 detainees, many of whom are civilians, with concerns raised about potential unfair trials due to coercive practices in security-related cases.  The move has been met with mixed reactions, with some Israelis supporting the tribunal while others call for a state commission of inquiry into the government's role in preventing the attack.

articles.title: Drugged, raped and filmed: German woman alleges years of horrific abuse by ex-partner - The Times of India
articles.rephrased_article: A German woman, 59-year-old Claudia Wuttke, has accused her former partner of drugging and raping her over a period of 16 years, with the alleged crimes captured on video.  Police discovered the videos in June 2025 after finding them on a laptop. The German authorities dropped investigations into 65 of the 67 alleged cases due to statute of limitations laws, leaving only two remaining cases for prosecution. Wuttke expressed her disappointment at the lack of justice and called it "unacceptable" that most of the abuse would go unpunished.

articles.title: ‘Kind of humiliating’: trans community responds to EHRC’s new code of practice | Gender | The Guardian
articles.rephrased_article: Stephen Whittle, a 70-year-old man who advocates for gender recognition, was at the Chelsea flower show when the updated code of practice from the Equality and Human Rights Commission was published. The guidance confirmed that single-sex spaces must be used based on biological sex, leading to mixed reactions. Some welcomed it as a consolidation of last year's court victory, while others expressed concern about its practical implications for trans inclusivity.  Businesses and service providers are grappling with the changes, seeking clarity and time to adapt their policies.

articles.title: ‘Most relentlessly cruel’: Gaza flotilla activists tell harrowing accounts of abuse in Israeli custody - World - DAWN.COM
articles.rephrased_article: Mousa Taher, a New Zealand activist, and other activists from the Global Sumud humanitarian aid flotilla, recounted harrowing experiences of abuse they endured while detained by Israeli forces.  Taher described being subjected to torture, including being bound tightly with plastic zip ties, having his face stepped on, and being beaten. He also said that Israeli soldiers recognized him and addressed him by name because he had previously been detained. Isselmou Ould Maloum, a Mauritanian activist, echoed similar accounts of violence, stating that the Israeli military lacks a strategy other than using force against Palestinians.  Gregory Terry, an American activist, described the detention as "miserable" and said his fellow activists suffered broken bones and were repeatedly tased. Juliet Lamont, an Australian activist, recounted being subjected to sexual assault and physical violence during their time on board the flotilla. All of these activists expressed their determination to continue protesting for Palestinian freedom.

articles.title: Flotilla video: Ben-Gvir’s template of televised abuse was honed on Palestinians | Israel | The Guardian
articles.rephrased_article: Itamar Ben-Gvir, Israel's national security minister, has been widely criticized for publicly celebrating abuse of detainees in Israeli jails.  He shared a video of the mistreatment of activists intercepted at sea attempting to deliver aid to Gaza, prompting condemnation from numerous countries and even the US ambassador to Israel. While Benjamin Netanyahu, the Israeli Prime Minister, condemned Ben-Gvir's actions, he has previously failed to address systemic abuse against Palestinians in custody.  This incident highlights a pattern of escalating violence and human rights violations against Palestinians under his leadership, with calls for sanctions and international intervention growing louder.

articles.title: Gaza flotilla activists allege abuse by Israeli forces while detained
articles.rephrased_article: Canadian Foreign Minister Anita Anand confirmed that her officials have received information detailing the "appalling abuse" of Canadian citizens detained in Israel following the interception of a Gaza-bound aid flotilla. Germany and Spain also reported injuries among their nationals, while organizers of the Global Sumud Flotilla alleged at least 15 cases of sexual assaults and other mistreatment.  The Israeli prison service dismissed the allegations as false, stating all detainees were held in accordance with the law.

articles.title: From Palestine to Catalonia, Guardiola believed in more than just football | Football News | Al Jazeera
articles.rephrased_article: Pep Guardiola, the legendary Manchester City manager, is stepping down after a decade of success.  He has used his platform to advocate for various causes beyond football, including Palestinian children in Gaza and homelessness in the UK. His outspokenness on these issues, while widely praised, also drew criticism from some groups, particularly regarding his comments about the Jewish community. Guardiola's legacy extends far beyond trophies won, as he has consistently used his influence to speak up for social justice.

articles.title: Gaza flotilla activists allege sexual assault and rape in Israeli detention | Israel | The Guardian
articles.rephrased_article: Activists released from Israeli custody following their detention on a flotilla attempting to deliver aid to Gaza have alleged abuse, including sexual assaults and injuries.  Israel’s prison service denies the allegations, stating all detainees are treated in accordance with the law and medical care is provided according to professional judgment. Several countries, including Germany, Italy, and France, reported injuries and accusations of serious misconduct, prompting investigations into possible crimes like kidnapping and sexual assault.  The incident has further strained relations between Israel and international organizations and governments.

articles.title: Ebola risk now at highest level in DR Congo, says WHO - World - DAWN.COM
articles.rephrased_article: The World Health Organisation (WHO) has raised the risk assessment level for the Ebola outbreak in the Democratic Republic of Congo to very high, citing a rapidly spreading epidemic with nearly 750 suspected cases and 177 suspected deaths.  Tedros Adhanom Ghebreyesus, WHO chief, emphasized the urgency of containing the virus, particularly due to violence and insecurity hindering response efforts. While Uganda's situation is stable, WHO has deployed international staff and prioritized existing treatments like monoclonal antibodies and olibdesivir for clinical trials.

articles.title: Deepa Jewellers, Cotec Healthcare receive Sebi approval for IPOs - The Economic Times
articles.rephrased_article: Deepa Jewellers, a Hyderabad-based company specializing in hallmarked gold jewelry processing and trading, plans to raise funds through an IPO consisting of a fresh issue and offer-for-sale. The IPO will include up to Rs 250 crore worth of shares from the company and up to 1.18 crore shares offered for sale by promoters Ashish Agarwal and Seema Agarwal.  Cotec Healthcare, a contract development and manufacturing organization (CDMO) serving pharmaceutical companies, also received Sebi approval for its IPO. The company manufactures formulations across various therapeutic segments and operates a manufacturing facility in Roorkee with an installed capacity of over 4 billion units.

articles.title: Gaza flotilla activists allege abuse, sexual assault in Israeli detention | Israel-Palestine conflict News | Al Jazeera
articles.rephrased_article: Global Sumud Flotilla organizers allege at least 15 cases of sexual assault and other abuse against freed activists who were abducted from international waters by Israeli forces. The allegations, which include claims of being stripped, kicked, tasered, and denied access to a lawyer, have been reported by activists who returned to their home countries and are under investigation by authorities in Italy, Germany, and Spain.  The Israeli prison service denies the allegations, stating that all detainees are held according to the law with full regard for their basic rights.

articles.title: Kim Soo-hyun: AI used to fake evidence that ended South Korean actor's career, say police
articles.rephrased_article: South Korean police are seeking an arrest warrant for a YouTuber, Kim Se-ui, who allegedly faked evidence to defame actor Kim Soo-hyun. The YouTuber manipulated screenshots of text messages and shared an audio file made with AI to falsely portray the actor as having dated actress Kim Sae-ron when she was underage.  The allegations led to Kim Soo-hyun's career downfall, prompting him to seek legal action against the YouTuber and the actress' family.

articles.title: Tanzanian police official Faustine Mafwele sanctioned by US for alleged human rights abuses
articles.rephrased_article: The US has sanctioned Faustine Jackson Mafwele, a senior Tanzanian police official, for alleged involvement in the torture and sexual assault of rights activists Boniface Mwangi and Agather Atuhaire.  This action comes amid growing scrutiny of Tanzania's human rights record, with US lawmakers calling for tougher action against the government. The sanctions bar Mafwele from entering the US, while Tanzania's Foreign Affairs Minister Mahmoud Thabit Kombo stated that the government has yet to receive the formal designation.  The US State Department cited "credible information" linking Mafwele to gross human rights violations, and Amnesty International previously called for an investigation into the activists' detention and alleged abuse.

articles.title: "She is going to end up in jail again": Asmongold fires back after Nina Lin blames him for spending night in jail over $4 scissors - The Times of India
articles.rephrased_article: Nina Lin and Asmongold engaged in a heated online dispute after Lin accused Asmongold of being involved in a situation that led to her spending the night in jail.  Lin claimed she accidentally failed to scan a pair of scissors at a self-checkout counter, leading to police involvement. Asmongold, who was shown clips of the incident during his livestream, responded by calling Lin's accusations baseless and predicting further trouble for her. The exchange has sparked widespread debate within Twitch, Kick, and X communities.

articles.title: Calcutta HC orders setting up SIT of CBI to probe hushing up charges in R G Kar rape-murder case - The Hindu
articles.rephrased_article: The Calcutta High Court ordered the creation of a three-member special investigation team (SIT) from the CBI to investigate the death of a trainee doctor at the RG Kar Medical College and Hospital. The court's decision follows allegations that evidence was destroyed and attempts were made to downplay the incident. The SIT will focus on the events leading up to the victim's cremation, including potential lapses in the initial investigation by both police and hospital authorities.  The team is expected to file a comprehensive report by June 25th.

articles.title: Boys convicted of rape get non-custodial sentences as judge says they should not be criminalised unnecessarily | UK news | The Guardian
articles.rephrased_article: Three teenage boys, aged 13 to 14 at the time of their crimes, were sentenced to youth rehabilitation orders ranging from 18 months to three years for their roles in a series of knife-point rapes and sexual assaults against two teenage girls. Judge Nicholas Rowland stated he wanted to support the boys' reintegration into society and avoid criminalising them unnecessarily due to their young age, low intelligence, and limited understanding of consent.  The judge acknowledged the seriousness of the crimes but emphasized that they were "very young" and had not been in any big trouble before. Donna Jones, Hampshire’s police and crime commissioner, expressed concern over the lenient sentences, stating they offer little comfort to the victims.

articles.title: Who are the 10 best FIFA World Cup players of all time? | World Cup 2026 | Al Jazeera
articles.rephrased_article: Zinedine Zidane, Jimmy Greaves, Ferenc Puskas, Lothar Matthaus, Miroslav Klose, Ronaldo, Franz Beckenbauer, Johan Cruyff, Diego Maradona, and Pele are considered among the best FIFA World Cup players of all time.  They have achieved success on the field, both individually and with their national teams. Some, like Zidane, Greaves, and Beckenbauer, have also been recognized for their leadership and contributions to the sport.

articles.title: Ebola: US ban on travellers from DRC, Uganda or South Sudan ‘not the solution’ | Global development | The Guardian
articles.rephrased_article: The World Health Organization (WHO) declared a public health emergency of international concern due to the ongoing Ebola outbreak in the Democratic Republic of Congo, with new cases reported in South Kivu province.  Africa Centers for Disease Control and Prevention (Africa CDC) criticized travel bans imposed by the US on citizens from the affected countries, arguing that they are ineffective and could exacerbate the situation. Dr Githinji Gitahi, CEO of Amref Health Africa, echoed this sentiment, emphasizing the need for investment in outbreak control at the source rather than isolating affected regions.  Uganda’s information minister, Chris Baryomunsi, countered by stating that his country has experience managing similar outbreaks and possesses the capacity to contain them.

articles.title: UK grooming case: 20 jailed for 277 years over rape and abuse of girls between 1995 and 2003 - The Times of India
articles.rephrased_article: Twenty individuals have been sentenced to a combined 277 years in prison for their roles in a child sexual abuse investigation spanning from 1995 to 2003. Sajid Majid, Manaf Hussain, and Tariq Azam received the longest sentences, with Majid receiving 28 years for five counts of rape and three counts of indecent assault.  The Kirklees District Police described the investigation as exposing "truly appalling sexual abuse" carried out by "a large number of sexual predators." Detective Chief Inspector Rob Stevens praised the victims' courage in enduring lengthy trials.

articles.title: Indian-origin truck driver Shamsher Singh jailed for 6 years for raping woman he met on dating app in New Zealand - The Times of India
articles.rephrased_article: Shamsher Singh, a 33-year-old Indian-origin man, was sentenced to six years and nine months in prison for raping a woman he met on a dating app during a late-night freight run. Singh assaulted the victim inside his commercial truck while parked on a remote stretch of highway between Nelson and Blenheim in January 2024. The victim accepted an invitation from Singh to accompany him on a delivery after connecting online and meeting for lunch in Nelson.  The assault occurred during the return leg of the journey, with the victim being asleep inside the vehicle when Singh attacked her.  Judge Harrop noted that Singh ignored the victim's distress and showed no remorse, resulting in the full sentence.

articles.title: Bolivian president to reshuffle cabinet amid antigovernment protests | Protests News | Al Jazeera
articles.rephrased_article: President Rodrigo Paz of Bolivia announced he will reorganize his cabinet in response to weeks of antigovernment protests and economic turmoil.  He stated the goal is to create a cabinet that can better address the concerns of protesters, who have taken to the streets to express frustration with his free-market reforms. The protests, which include demonstrations by farmers, laborers, miners, and teachers, have been met with clashes between riot police and demonstrators. Former President Evo Morales, who continues to exert influence over Bolivian politics, has voiced support for the protesters.  The US Secretary of State Marco Rubio has also expressed support for Paz, while Colombia's President Gustavo Petro criticized the protests as a "popular insurrection" and called for dialogue.

articles.title: Israeli security minister stirs diplomatic outrage with flotilla activist abuse video | Israel | The Guardian
articles.rephrased_article: Itamar Ben-Gvir, Israel’s national security minister, sparked a diplomatic crisis by publishing footage of Israeli security forces abusing activists detained while attempting to sail to Gaza with aid. The video drew condemnation from countries whose citizens were onboard the boats, including the UK, Canada, Germany, the Netherlands, Spain, and Ireland. Mike Huckabee, the US ambassador to Israel, called Ben-Gvir’s behavior “despicable,” while Giorgia Meloni, Italy’s prime minister, demanded the release of all Italian citizens involved and an apology for the mistreatment.  Winston Peters, New Zealand's foreign affairs minister, condemned Ben-Gvir’s actions and placed a travel ban on him in 2025. The activists were detained after their boats were intercepted while attempting to break the Israeli blockade of Gaza. Rights groups documented widespread abuse and torture of Palestinians by Israeli authorities during the recent conflict.

articles.title: Tens of thousands turn out for UK far-right rally, counter protest - World - DAWN.COM
articles.rephrased_article: Tens of thousands attended a rally organized by far-right activist Tommy Robinson in London, where he urged attendees to be "peaceful and courteous."  A counter-demonstration, combining with an anti-fascism march organized by the Stand Up to Racism group, drew smaller crowds. The Metropolitan Police deployed 4,000 officers for the event, citing concerns about potential clashes between rival groups and a heightened threat level due to recent violent attacks targeting London's Jewish community.  Elon Musk, owner of X (formerly Twitter), addressed Robinson's rally last September via video-link. Prime Minister Keir Starmer condemned the organizers of Robinson's rally, accusing them of "peddling hatred and division."

articles.title: Remove Bandi Sanjay from Union Cabinet, Kavitha tells Modi - The Hindu
articles.rephrased_article: Kalvakuntla Kavitha, president of the Telangana Rakshana Sena, urged Prime Minister Narendra Modi to remove Union Minister of State for Home Affairs Bandi Sanjay Kumar from his position until the investigation and trial in the POCSO case involving his son are complete.  Kavitha expressed concern over potential conflict of interest and a perception of political influence on the investigation, arguing that public trust in the justice system could be damaged by Mr. Kumar's continued presence in office.

articles.title: ‘Research here is world class’: son of Steve Jobs looks to invest in UK cancer care | Venture capital | The Guardian
articles.rephrased_article: Reed Jobs, a venture capitalist and the son of Apple co-founder Steve Jobs, is leading an oncology-focused venture capital fund called Yosemite, which has invested in over 20 healthcare startups.  The firm focuses on gene therapy, cancer vaccines, radiopharmaceuticals, and artificial intelligence, with a goal of making cancer treatable and non-lethal. Yosemite receives funding from organizations like LifeArc, a UK-based not-for-profit focused on rare diseases, and has partnerships with universities like Oxford and Cambridge.  Jobs hopes to see a shift in cancer care towards early diagnosis and personalized treatment similar to advances made with HIV and cardiovascular disease.

articles.title: UK police brace for far-right rally and counter-demonstration - World - DAWN.COM
articles.rephrased_article: Thousands of people gathered in London for two opposing demonstrations: a far-right rally organized by Tommy Robinson and a counter-demonstration combining pro-Palestinian and anti-fascist sentiments. The Metropolitan Police deployed 4,000 officers to manage the events, citing concerns about potential violence and clashes between rival groups.  The Met has imposed strict conditions on both rallies, including restrictions on routes and timings, in an effort to keep attendees separated. Elon Musk, owner of X (formerly Twitter), addressed a similar rally organized by Robinson last year, drawing large crowds and sparking controversy.

articles.title: Cyberabad police begin search for Bandi Bageerath in Hyderabad and Karimnagar after HC rejects pre-arrest bail plea - The Hindu
articles.rephrased_article: Cyberabad police intensified their search for Bandi Bageerath, accused of sexually assaulting and emotionally manipulating a 17-year-old girl, by conducting searches at his residences in Hyderabad and Karimnagar.  Five police teams were involved in the operation, which included physical checks and surveillance efforts to track his whereabouts. The investigation is ongoing, with discussions about Bageerath surrendering to authorities before being subjected to medical examination and remanded.

articles.title: Meghalaya: Looking beyond the grape | Market demand for fruit wines and an enabling government policy is motivating small-time winemakers to go commercial - The Hindu
articles.rephrased_article: Lyang B. Sangma, an entrepreneur from Meghalaya, is excited about the potential of his te.gism fruit wine after it was selected by the Meghalaya Farmers Empowerment Commission (MFEC) to be showcased at Vinexpo India 2024 in Mumbai. The MFEC chose six exotic fruit wines and meads for the event, including Sangma's te.gism product, which has gained recognition from experts and connoisseurs beyond his hometown of Tura.

articles.title: What China critics in Maga movement make of Trump's Beijing trip
articles.rephrased_article: Donald Trump's visit to Beijing, following a decade of anti-China rhetoric from his administration, saw a softening of his stance towards the Chinese government.  While he hailed "fantastic trade deals" and called Xi Jinping his friend, hardline positions within the Republican Party remained. The trip included limited concessions on trade, with approvals for Nvidia and Boeing, but no concrete details were provided regarding Taiwan or the $14 billion arms sale to Taiwan that remains a point of contention between the US and China.  Despite this, Trump's approach is expected to influence other officials and lawmakers, potentially leading to a shift in policy towards China.

articles.title: Quote of the day by Galileo Galilei: “There are those who reason well, but they are greatly outnumbered by those who reason badly.”
articles.rephrased_article: Galileo Galilei's quote, "There are those who reason well, but they are greatly outnumbered by those who reason badly," has resurfaced online due to its relevance to the current climate of misinformation and emotional reasoning. The quote reflects a timeless truth about human behavior: that thoughtful reasoning often struggles against the prevalence of irrational thinking, particularly in large groups where emotions drive opinions.  This observation resonates with people today who face constant bombardment of emotionally charged information, making it difficult to discern fact from fiction. Despite its pessimistic tone, the quote offers a glimmer of hope by highlighting that thoughtful questioning and evidence-based reasoning still exist even amidst overwhelming noise.

articles.title: HC denies pre-arrest bail to Bandi Sanjay’s son, reserves order - The Hindu
articles.rephrased_article: The Telangana High Court declined to grant pre-arrest bail to Union Minister of State for Home Affairs Bandi Sanjay's son, Sai Bageerath, in a POCSO Act case.  Justice T. Madhavi Devi reserved orders on the anticipatory bail petition and will pronounce them on May 21st. The judge heard arguments from both sides, with senior counsel S. Niranjan Reddy arguing that the relationship between the accused and the victim was amicable and the alleged offense might not be as severe as suggested in the FIR. Advocate Pappu Nageshwar Rao representing the victim's mother opposed the bail plea citing Supreme Court judgments rejecting anticipatory bails in POCSO cases and highlighting the trauma experienced by the victim. The Public Prosecutor for Home Palle Nageshwar Rao refuted the arguments of the petitioner’s counsel regarding an improvement in the FIR.

articles.title: 'No evidence you suffered in India': Inside Sanaullah Khan Mohammed's failed attempt to get asylum in US
articles.rephrased_article: A US Court of Appeals for the Seventh Circuit denied asylum to Sanaullah Khan Mohammed, an Indian Muslim man who entered the US on a tourist visa in 2016 and overstayed. The court found no merit in his claim of persecution in India, citing that local police intervened in the incident he described and that the slaughterhouse business he claimed was the source of tension is no longer operating.  The court also ruled that Mohammed could be deported to any location within India as it is a large country.

articles.title: 50 Green Card holders identified to be deported as US starts re-vetting older cases
articles.rephrased_article: The Department of Homeland Security has established a new unit, the "Tactical Operations Division," to re-vet Green Card applications. The unit, headed by Daniel Andrade, has identified at least 50 individuals through its review process and found that 80% of those cases were clean, requiring no further action.  Experts argue that this exercise is meaningless as Green Cards are already subject to extensive vetting. However, the unit can potentially lead to deportation for those convicted of crimes or who obtained their status fraudulently.

articles.title: Another mistrial declared in Harvey Weinstein rape retrial
articles.rephrased_article: Harvey Weinstein was declared guilty of rape in a New York trial, but the verdict was overturned. The judge declared a mistrial after the jury failed to reach a unanimous decision on whether he raped aspiring actress Jessica Mann in a hotel room over a decade ago. This is the third time a New York jury has considered this case against the 74-year-old disgraced film mogul, who remains jailed on other charges.

articles.title: New York Times defends journalist after Israel threatens to sue
articles.rephrased_article: The New York Times responded to a libel threat from Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu regarding an article alleging sexual assault against Palestinian detainees by Israeli security services. The newspaper stated the claim is "without merit" and accused Israel's foreign minister Gideon Saar of using a "distorted lie" to undermine independent reporting.  The article, written by Nicholas Kristof, detailed accounts from alleged victims and cited reports from NGOs alleging sexual violence against Palestinians in detention. While Israel's ambassador to the US expressed disapproval and Jewish protesters demonstrated outside the New York Times office, legal experts suggest a successful libel suit would be challenging due to Israeli defamation laws.

articles.title: Imam, 54, who claimed ‘jinn powers’ jailed for life over abuse crimes against women and girls
articles.rephrased_article: Abdul Halim Khan, a former imam in East London, was sentenced to life imprisonment for 21 sexual offences against seven victims. The judge condemned his abuse of trust as "monstrous" and noted that he used supernatural claims to manipulate victims who were vulnerable due to their faith. Prosecutors highlighted the use of fear and isolation tactics by Khan to silence victims, allowing him to continue abusing them for nearly a decade.  The case has sparked national discussions about safeguarding failures within religious institutions and the challenges faced by victims coming forward.

articles.title: Israel threatens to sue New York Times over report on sexual abuse of Palestinian inmates - World - DAWN.COM
articles.rephrased_article: Israel's Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu and Foreign Minister Gideon Saar have threatened to sue The New York Times over a column by Nicholas Kristof alleging widespread sexual abuse of Palestinian detainees. The Israeli government claims the article is based on unverified sources and that it was published to undermine an independent report on alleged Hamas sexual violence.  The New York Times maintains the lawsuit lacks merit and argues the claim is part of a political strategy to silence reporting that doesn't align with the narrative.

articles.title: Explosions heard as mining groups stage antigovernment protest in Bolivia | Protests News | Al Jazeera
articles.rephrased_article: Protesters in Bolivia, led by mining groups and rural unions, clashed with law enforcement during a demonstration demanding the resignation of President Rodrigo Paz. The unrest followed weeks of road blockades as Bolivians express frustration over the country's economic crisis, which has seen soaring inflation, supply shortages, and higher prices.  The government, while open to dialogue, has refused demands for President Paz’s resignation.  Some of his allies have blamed former President Evo Morales, who continues to draw popular support in rural areas, for the unrest.

articles.title: Israel says it will sue New York Times over article on sexual abuse of Palestinian prisoners | Israel | The Guardian
articles.rephrased_article: Benjamin Netanyahu, Gideon Sa’ar, and the Israeli Ministry of Foreign Affairs have threatened to sue The New York Times for defamation over an essay by Nicholas Kristof detailing allegations of sexual abuse in Israeli military detention.  The officials claim the reporting is a "blood libel" and that it defames soldiers, while the New York Times has defended its reporting as accurate and corroborated with multiple sources. Legal experts believe such a lawsuit would be without merit and are unlikely to succeed in any court.

articles.title: Woman gang-raped inside bus in Delhi’s Rani Bagh, two arrested - The Hindu
articles.rephrased_article: Police in Rani Bagh have arrested two bus drivers, Umesh Kumar and Ramender, for the gang-rape of a woman on a private sleeper bus. The assault occurred on May 11th after the woman refused to engage with the men following a monetary agreement.  The woman reported the incident to the police who seized the vehicle used in the crime. Both accused were apprehended within hours of the incident being reported and an FIR has been filed.

articles.title: Israel’s Netanyahu says suing New York Times over Palestinian rape article | Media News | Al Jazeera
articles.rephrased_article: Israel’s Prime Minister, Benjamin Netanyahu, and Foreign Minister, Gideon Saar, have instructed the initiation of a defamation lawsuit against The New York Times following an article by columnist Nicholas Kristof detailing alleged sexual violence by Israeli forces against Palestinian detainees. The report, based on accounts from 14 victims, has been met with strong condemnation from Israel, which calls it "lies" and a "blood libel".  The newspaper maintains its reporting is accurate and stands by the article's factual basis.  However, critics question the publication of the piece under the "opinion" section while similar reports on alleged abuses against Israelis have been published as "news."

articles.title: Paediatrician in Germany charged with 130 counts of sexual abuse | Germany | The Guardian
articles.rephrased_article: German prosecutors have charged a 46-year-old paediatrician with 130 counts of sexual abuse, including rape, committed between 2013 and 2025. The alleged crimes occurred at clinics operated by the Havelland healthcare group in Brandenburg state. The doctor is accused of abusing most of his patients while they were under his care.  The case has prompted investigations into safeguarding procedures at clinics across the region, with the Havelland Kliniken group pledging full support to prosecutors and providing any relevant information. A regional court will decide whether to proceed to trial.

articles.title: Israeli minister blasts Barcelona’s Lamine Yamal for Palestinian flag wave | World Cup 2026 News | Al Jazeera
articles.rephrased_article: Lamine Yamal, a 18-year-old Barcelona player, sparked controversy by waving a Palestinian flag during a victory parade celebrating the Spanish league title. Israel’s defense minister, Katz, criticized Yamal's actions, accusing him of inciting hate against Israel while soldiers combat Hamas in Gaza.  Yamal, who is Muslim, posted pictures of himself holding the flag on his Instagram account. The incident has drawn criticism from Spain's government and a large part of its population, which has been highly critical of Israel’s war in Gaza.

articles.title: Trump in China: Xi Jinping welcomes US president but thorny issues remain
articles.rephrased_article: President Donald Trump received a grand welcome from Xi Jinping in China, marking the first day of his visit that could reset ties between the two superpowers.  The event included military honors and praise from Trump, who called for increased economic cooperation with China. However, tensions remain over Taiwan and trade disputes, as well as the ongoing war in Iran. The visit aims to showcase China's growing influence while highlighting a potential shift in global power dynamics. While details of any agreements are still unclear, both leaders expressed a desire for a "constructive" relationship.

articles.title: DR Congo conflict: M23 and Rwanda accused of atrocities in Uvira
articles.rephrased_article: Human Rights Watch (HRW) investigators have documented widespread atrocities committed by the M23 rebel group and Rwandan soldiers during their occupation of Uvira, Democratic Republic of Congo. The report details the execution of 53 civilians, including children, through door-to-door raids, as well as eight cases of rape allegedly perpetrated by both groups. HRW also found evidence of forced recruitment, abductions, and enforced disappearances.  The organization believes these acts constitute war crimes and has called for accountability from the Rwandan government and the M23.

articles.title: Alien smuggling and child sexual abuse material: Iranian national pleads guilty in New York court to two serious federal crimes - The Times of India
articles.rephrased_article: A Sharon Gohari, a naturalized US citizen of Iranian descent, pleaded guilty to charges of alien smuggling and receiving child sexual abuse material in federal court.  Gohari operated a scheme from at least December 2020 until May 2025, facilitating travel for Iranian nationals seeking entry into the US for thousands of dollars per client. Authorities discovered child sexual abuse material on Gohari's phone, including videos depicting the rape of children as young as five years old, and he shared some with overseas accounts in Iran.  Sentencing is scheduled for a later date.

articles.title: Man arrested on suspicion of rape after woman alleges assault near church in Maidstone - The Times of India
articles.rephrased_article: Kent Police arrested a 50-year-old man on suspicion of rape following an alleged assault near a church in Maidstone. The incident occurred between 7 pm and 10 pm on Saturday, with the woman reporting the attack to police late that evening.  The suspect remains in custody while police continue their investigation, cordoning off the area and urging residents with CCTV or dashcams to check for footage.

articles.title: Behind TVK Vijay’s rise is a generation drawn to “cinematic politics” amid a growing crisis of purpose - The Hindu
articles.rephrased_article: Joseph Vijay, leader of the Tamilaga Vettri Kazhagam (TVK), won a significant number of seats in the recent Tamil Nadu election, capitalizing on a sense of restlessness and disillusionment among youth voters.  The victory was attributed to his ability to connect with young voters through a narrative of change that resonated with their desire for purpose and direction amidst routine life. This trend highlights the growing influence of social media and escapist entertainment in shaping political discourse and voter engagement, as evidenced by the TVK's successful campaign strategy.  However, critics argue that this "change" is superficial and lacks concrete solutions to address pressing issues like gender-based violence.

articles.title: Epstein abused me while under house arrest, survivor tells US lawmakers
articles.rephrased_article: A survivor of Jeffrey Epstein's abuse, Roza, testified before House Democrats in West Palm Beach, Florida, detailing how she was sexually abused while he was under house arrest.  Roza, who was recruited by Jean-Luc Brunel, Epstein's associate, said she was offered work to help with her financial troubles and that Epstein subjected her to rape over three years. The hearing, organized by Democratic lawmakers from the US House Oversight Committee, aimed to keep the Epstein case in the spotlight and highlight the failures of the justice system in holding him accountable.

articles.title: A society at large under question: rebuild a culture where safety of children is collective responsibility - The Hindu
articles.rephrased_article: A three- to four-year-old girl was allegedly sexually assaulted and murdered in Maharashtra's Pune district, highlighting the fragility of social trust and safety for children. The incident has prompted calls for a more comprehensive approach to dealing with repeat sexual offenders, including stricter parole restrictions, enhanced monitoring by law enforcement, and expedited justice processes.  The National Commission for Women is working closely with authorities to ensure a timely investigation and swift proceedings.

articles.title: Hamas 'weaponised' sexual violence in 7 October attacks, Israeli investigation says
articles.rephrased_article: An independent Israeli investigation has published a 300-page report detailing "systematic, widespread" sexual violence by Hamas and other Palestinian armed groups during the October 7th attacks. The report, based on interviews with survivors and attackers' footage, concludes that rapes, sexual assault, and torture were intended to inflict maximum pain and suffering.  The investigation also found evidence of gang rapes at a dance festival where over 370 people were killed, as well as the forced sexual acts on family members by captors. The report states that these crimes constitute war crimes, crimes against humanity, and genocidal acts under international law.

articles.title: Lorna Hajdini looks very attractive: Megyn Kelly says she believes Chirayu Rana made up the whole sexual assault lawsuit - The Times of India
articles.rephrased_article: Megyn Kelly and Michael Knowles weighed in on the sexual assault lawsuit against Chirayu Rana, with Kelly suggesting it is fabricated due to Lorna Hajdini's attractiveness.  They criticized Rana's alleged lies about his father's death and short employment history, while Knowles pointed out inconsistencies in a technical aspect of the lawsuit. The case will be heard by a New York state court on May 26th.

articles.title: Sexual assault case: child rights commission visits victim in Eluru - The Hindu
articles.rephrased_article: Andhra Pradesh State Commission for Protection of Child Rights (APSCPCR) chairperson Vetukuri A.V.S. Suryanarayana Raju and member V. Gandhi Babu visited a minor girl who was allegedly sexually abused by a pastor on Monday, May 11, 2026. They inquired with doctors about the girl's condition and assured the family of government support and protection.  Women Development and Child Welfare Department Joint Director Sujatha Rani, Eluru District Project Director Sarada, District Child Protection Officer Ch. Surya Chakraveni, and other officials accompanied the Commission.

articles.title: Senior cabinet ministers and more than 70 MPs call for Keir Starmer’s resignation as speech fails to quell rebellion – as it happened | Politics | The Guardian
articles.rephrased_article: Senior cabinet ministers urged Keir Starmer to set a timetable for his departure, as more than 70 Labour MPs called for him to resign. The pressure on Starmer intensified after he failed to quell criticism following bruising local election results and the resignation of several MPs.  Several cabinet members, including Yvette Cooper and Shabana Mahmood, expressed concerns about the leadership crisis and urged Starmer to consider his position. A number of Labour MPs, including Charlotte Nichols and Debbie Abrahams, publicly called for Starmer's resignation, citing public dissatisfaction with his leadership.  Melanie Ward, a Scottish Labour MP, resigned as Justice PPS, stating that constituents were unhappy with Starmer's leadership, while others, such as Rachel Taylor, expressed their support for him to continue leading the party.

articles.title: TCS Nashik case: NCW flags ‘toxic work culture’, ‘zero POSH compliance’ - The Hindu
articles.rephrased_article: The National Commission for Women (NCW) has found that Tata Consultancy Services (TCS) in Nashik is failing to comply with the Prevention of Sexual Harassment (POSH) Act, citing pervasive harassment, religious denigration, and systemic bullying. The NCW's fact-finding committee observed that victims were intimidated into silence due to a lack of formal complaint mechanisms and a toxic workplace environment.  The committee has recommended action for TCS’ failure to comply with the POSH Act, as well as measures to protect complainants and ensure a safe working environment.

articles.title: The road to deliver women’s safety - The Hindu
articles.rephrased_article: The case of Sai Bhagirath, son of Union Minister of State for Home Affairs Bandi Sanjay, under the Protection of Children from Sexual Offences (POCSO) Act is being closely watched as a test of how Telangana handles crimes against women and children. The state government has taken several steps to address online and offline harassment, including launching the "Stand with Her" initiative and investigating cases of cyberbullying. However, the case highlights the challenge of balancing free expression with curbing online targeting and harassment, particularly for women in positions of power.  The incident has sparked protests demanding action from both women's groups and political parties.

articles.title: Telangana BJP distances itself from POCSO case against Bandi Sanjay’s son, calls it legal issue - The Hindu
articles.rephrased_article: The Bharatiya Janata Party (BJP) in Telangana distanced itself from a POCSO case involving the son of Union Minister of State for Home Affairs, Bandi Sanjay Kumar. The state BJP president, N. Ramchander Rao, stated that the party has no connection to the matter and will investigate if any family member is involved.  Rao also addressed allegations of discrepancies in the Special Intensive Revision (SIR) conducted during the recent Assembly elections, claiming it was a clean-up exercise approved by the Election Commission and Supreme Court. He asserted that the SIR aimed to eliminate "bogus" voters and that the results reflected the mandate of genuine voters.

articles.title: Bandi Bhagirath’s case takes serious turn with Telangana CM ordering special team for comprehensive probe - The Hindu
articles.rephrased_article: A. Revanth Reddy, Telangana Chief Minister, has demanded an immediate investigation into allegations of sexual harassment against the son of Union Minister of State for Home Affairs Bandi Sanjay Kumar, Bandi Bhagirath.  The Chief Minister, who is also the Home Minister, instructed the Director General of Police (DGP), C.V. Anand, to launch a probe into the case registered at Pet Basheerabad Police Station. The investigation follows allegations that the police have been slow to act on the complaint lodged by the alleged victim on May 8th.

articles.title: Bandi urges BJP workers to not believe allegations - The Hindu
articles.rephrased_article: Bandi Sanjay Kumar, Union Minister of State for Home Affairs, addressed allegations against him and his family, stating he would never engage in actions that harm the BJP.  He urged his supporters to disregard the accusations made by the Bharat Rashtra Samithi (BRS).

articles.title: Sub-inspector suspended - The Hindu
articles.rephrased_article: Mujeeb H., a sub-inspector at the Elamakkara police station, was suspended on Sunday after being booked in two separate cases for sexual harassment, intimidation, and attempted extortion. The alleged incidents occurred in 2025, involving misuse of a narcotics investigation to obtain a woman's phone number and make sexual advances. H. is currently absconding.

articles.title: BRS leader Praveen Kumar demands SIT probe with women police officers into POCSO case against Bandi Sanjay’s son - The Hindu
articles.rephrased_article: R.S. Praveen Kumar, general secretary of the Bharat Rashtra Samithi (BRS), has called for a Special Investigation Team (SIT) with senior women police officers to investigate the high-profile POCSO case against the son of Union Minister of State for Home Bandi Sanjay.  Kumar stated that the police delayed accepting the complaint from the victim's family for five hours and did not provide an acknowledgement until they threatened suicide at a meeting with the Prime Minister.

articles.title: Research sheds light on GI’s murder of seven-year-old girl in Northern Ireland in 1944 | Northern Ireland | The Guardian
articles.rephrased_article: On September 25, 1944, William Harrison, a US soldier stationed in Northern Ireland, raped and murdered seven-year-old Patsy Wylie.  Annie Kalotschke, Patsy's niece, has spent decades researching the case and uncovering new details about the crime. Her research revealed that Harrison was disciplined for drunkenness and amnesia before being posted to a reserve combat unit in Northern Ireland. The execution of Harrison was botched, with the rope strangling him for 20 minutes instead of causing a swift death.  Kalotschke's findings have brought new understanding and closure to the case and its impact on the Wylie family.

articles.title: Rupali Chakankar appears before SIT in 'godman' Kharat case - The Hindu
articles.rephrased_article: Rupali Chakankar, NCP leader and former State women’s panel chief, appeared before the special investigation team (SIT) in Nashik to answer questions about her alleged association with self-styled godman Ashok Kharat.  Ms. Chakankar resigned from both positions following revelations of her ties to Kharat, who is currently under arrest for rape and sexual exploitation. The Maharashtra Government has set up an SIT to investigate 12 cases against Kharat in Nashik and Ahilyanagar districts, with the SIT likely to question Ms. Chakankar about her connection to him.  Senior Congress leader Nana Patole alleged that Kharat’s life is in danger in prison and demanded the removal of four ministers connected to him from the state cabinet.

articles.title: This is the sentence that protects every abuser in Pakistan - Pakistan - DAWN.COM
articles.rephrased_article: A pervasive societal stigma, "Sharif aurat thaney nahi jaati," prevents women from seeking justice at police stations in Pakistan. This belief system, often fueled by family pressure and a fear of social repercussions, discourages women from reporting domestic violence, harassment, or other crimes. Despite the existence of legal frameworks like the Domestic Violence (Prevention and Protection) Act and provisions within the Pakistan Penal Code, many women choose to avoid seeking help at police stations due to this ingrained prejudice.  This societal barrier hinders the ability of law enforcement institutions to effectively address the widespread issue of violence against women.

articles.title: Eluru pastor arrested under POCSO Act for sexual assault of minor - The Hindu
articles.rephrased_article: Chavatapalli Rambabu alias Hosanna, a prayer house operator in Eluru district, has been arrested for allegedly raping and impregnating a minor girl. The girl's mother reported the incident to police, alleging that Rambabu gave her daughter a heavy dose of pills to terminate the pregnancy. Eluru District Superintendent of Police K. Pratap Shiva Kishore confirmed the arrest under the POCSO Act and other relevant sections.  The accused will be produced in court.

articles.title: Pallegama Hemarathana Thero: Buddhist monk arrested for alleged rape of teen in Sri Lanka
articles.rephrased_article: Venerable Pallegama Hemarathana Thero, a high-ranking Buddhist monk and chief prelate of eight sacred sites in Sri Lanka, has been arrested for the alleged rape and sexual assault of a 15-year-old girl. The arrest followed criticism from the country's child protection authority regarding police inaction against him.  The monk is currently awaiting trial on May 12th. His mother was also arrested and remanded to custody for aiding and abetting the abuse.

articles.title: Chirayu Rana's attorney says he did not fake father's death, it was about a 'dad-like figure' - The Times of India
articles.rephrased_article: Chirayu Rana, a former JPMorgan Chase employee, is embroiled in controversy after filing a lawsuit against Lorna Hajdini, alleging sexual harassment.  Rana's attorney, Daniel Kaiser, denies the allegations and claims attempts are being made to defame his client. Rana has worked for several financial institutions including Carlyle Group, Morgan Stanley, and Apollo Global Management, before joining JPMorgan Chase in 2024. The lawsuit alleges that Hajdini invited a witness to a threesome, which prompted Rana's withdrawal of the initial complaint but was later refiled.

articles.title: Police to step up surveillance of abandoned properties as rape attempt case renews safety fears - The Hindu
articles.rephrased_article: Kochi City police have launched a mission to identify and monitor vulnerable spots that could become criminal shelters following a recent rape attempt in an abandoned building.  The incident, which involved three men attacking a woman after her male friend was held at knifepoint, has raised concerns about the safety risks posed by abandoned buildings, overgrown premises, and poorly lit areas across the city. District Police Chief (Kochi City) Kaliraj Mahesh Kumar said police teams have been conducting inspections to assess security risks.

articles.title: Soil testing at California house turns up evidence of human remains in Kirstin Smart case | California | The Guardian
articles.rephrased_article: San Luis Obispo County Sheriff Ian Parkinson announced that soil testing at a property linked to Paul Flores, convicted of Kristin Smart's murder, revealed evidence of human remains.  The remains are not yet identified as Smart's but support the presence of human remains at one time. Ruben Flores, Paul's father, was acquitted of accessory charges in 2022. The search of the property belonging to Susan Flores, Paul's mother, is ongoing and will continue until all avenues have been exhausted.

articles.title: Officer who cracked serial rapist Worboys case says justice system ‘close to exploding’ | Crime | The Guardian
articles.rephrased_article: Tim Grattan-Kane, the former senior investigating officer in the John Worboys case, believes similar crimes could still be happening today due to an overstretched justice system. He cites a lack of support workers and funding issues within the Crown Prosecution Service as contributing factors.  Grattan-Kane also points to the Gisèle Pelicot case in France and the Vikas Nath trial in London as examples of ongoing drink spiking incidents, highlighting the need for continued awareness and victim support. The Metropolitan Police has acknowledged its past mistakes in handling Worboys' case but has since adopted a more survivor-focused approach.

articles.title: Pastor sexual assault case: Commission to visit house of the victim in Andhra Pradesh - The Hindu
articles.rephrased_article: The Andhra Pradesh State Commission for Protection of Child Rights (APSCPCR) has taken suo motu cognizance of the alleged sexual assault and abuse of a minor girl by Church Pastor Choutapalli Rambabu in Kamavarapukota mandal. The commission is investigating reports that the victim was administered excessive dosage of abortion pills, leading to severe health complications.  The incident has sparked widespread concern across the state.

articles.title: ‘The worst kind of predator’: Louisiana pastor found guilty of sexually molesting two teen boys | New Orleans | The Guardian
articles.rephrased_article: Terry Reed, a 66-year-old suburban New Orleans pastor, was convicted of sexually molesting two minors. Reed had previously been convicted in 1997 and 2017 for indecent behavior with juveniles and molestation of a juvenile, respectively. Prosecutors argued that he preyed on troubled boys lacking a father figure and exploited his position as a religious leader to abuse them. The jury deliberated for less than an hour before finding Reed guilty of two counts each of third-degree rape and molestation of a juvenile. He faces up to 25 years in prison for the rape convictions and between five and 40 years for the molestation charges.

articles.title: Power blazer? Victoria Starmer marks key political moment in cream | Fashion | The Guardian
articles.rephrased_article: Victoria Starmer, accompanied by her husband, the Prime Minister, wore a cream blazer to vote on Thursday morning. This follows a trend of high-profile women like Princess of Wales, Amanda Holden, and Melania Trump who have also embraced the power blazer in recent years. The blazer is considered a symbol of authority and competence, offering a neutral color that stands out while signaling professionalism.  The cream hue has been adopted by politicians and business leaders as a way to project confidence and approachability.

articles.title: 126 MLAs-elect in T.N. have criminal cases pending against them; TVK tops list with 41 - The Hindu
articles.rephrased_article: The Association for Democratic Reforms (ADR) and Tamil Nadu Election Watch (TNEW) released a report analyzing the criminal backgrounds of 234 winning candidates in the April 2026 Tamil Nadu Assembly elections. The report found that at least 126 candidates, including those from the Tamilaga Vettri Kazhagam (TVK), have pending criminal cases against them.  The TVK had the highest number of candidates with pending cases, followed by the DMK, AIADMK, and PMK. The report also noted that serious criminal cases include offences involving assault, murder, kidnap, or rape, as well as offenses related to loss to the exchequer.

articles.title: Barrister says ‘dead woman was put on trial’ after husband cleared of manslaughter | Violence against women and girls | The Guardian
articles.rephrased_article: A jury acquitted Christopher Trybus of all charges, including manslaughter, coercive and controlling behavior, two counts of rape, after a trial that centered around the death of his wife, Tarryn Baird.  Charlotte Proudman, a family law barrister who did not attend the trial, criticized the defense's closing arguments, calling it "Kafkaesque" and suggesting the prosecution had an agenda. The defense countered that the case was based on false allegations and compared the situation to the French Revolution and the film "Chicago." Katy Thorne, Trybus's barrister, defended the defense's approach and argued that the prosecution was not properly addressing the rare nature of false allegations.  The Crown Prosecution Service (CPS) has said it will consider bringing cases where there is evidence to do so after a jury found Trybus not guilty.

articles.title: POCSO case booked against Minister Bandi Sanjay’s son after minor’s complaint - The Hindu
articles.rephrased_article: Bandi Sanjay, Union Minister of State for Home Affairs, and his son Bandi Bhageerath are facing separate allegations.  A 17-year-old girl filed a POCSO Act complaint against Bhageerath alleging sexual assault at a farmhouse in Moinabad on December 31st.  Bhageerath subsequently filed a blackmail complaint against the girl's family, but the girl's family countered with their own accusation of sexual assault. Both complaints are being investigated separately.

articles.title: ​Take east: On the BJP government in West Bengal - The Hindu
articles.rephrased_article: The Bharatiya Janata Party (BJP) secured a resounding victory in the West Bengal Assembly elections, winning 207 out of 294 seats.  Suvendu Adhikari, former Leader of the Opposition and now the new Chief Minister, defeated incumbent Mamata Banerjee in her own constituency, marking a significant shift in power dynamics. The BJP's success can be attributed to its strategic focus on booth-level organization, leveraging Hindu identity politics, and exploiting popular dissatisfaction with the TMC's governance.  The party's victory comes with challenges, including restoring law and order after targeted violence.

articles.title: Prisons report 98.33% pass in Class 12 State board exams - The Hindu
articles.rephrased_article: Tamil Nadu's Department of Prisons and Correctional Services reported a 98.33% pass rate in the Class XII board examinations, with all three top scorers being prisoners at the Central Prison, Palayamkottai.  The Tamil Nadu School Education Department established examination centers within prisons based on requests from prison officials. The top three scorers were P. Vinith (549 marks), T. Manikandan (531 marks), and B. Balu (527 marks).

articles.title: Congress slams Modi Government over women’s safety citing NCRB data - The Hindu
articles.rephrased_article: Congress party leaders, including Mallikarjun Kharge, criticized the Narendra Modi Government for its handling of women's safety and rising crime rates.  Kharge cited data from the National Crime Records Bureau (NCRB) showing a significant increase in crimes against women, children, Dalits, Adivasis, and cybercrime during the past decade. He accused the government of using "Beti Bachao" and "Nari Vandan" as mere slogans while failing to address these issues effectively. Alka Lamba, president of the All India Mahila Congress, echoed these concerns, alleging that the BJP was shielding perpetrators instead of ensuring justice for victims.

articles.title: Sexual harassment more than twice as prevalent at England’s top universities, analysis finds | Students | The Guardian
articles.rephrased_article: A national survey of undergraduates revealed that students at high tariff universities, those requiring the highest A-level grades for entry, were more than twice as likely to experience sexual harassment compared to those at lower tariff institutions.  The analysis by the Office for Students, England's higher education regulator, found hotspots of sexual harassment and violence in courses like medicine, dentistry, veterinary sciences or languages. Jo Grady, general secretary of the University and College Union, expressed concern that perpetrators from these prestigious universities could perpetuate toxic cultures while Prof Libby Hackett, chief executive of the Russell Group, acknowledged the need for continued efforts to ensure student safety on campus.

articles.title: Senators alarmed by ‘surge’ in violence against women; 5pc conviction rate termed ‘systemic failure’ - Pakistan - DAWN.COM
articles.rephrased_article: Senators expressed alarm over a surge in violence against women, including honor killings, and called for stronger measures to improve conviction rates.  The presiding officer of the Senate, Sherry Rehman, stated that the current five percent conviction rate reflected a "systemic failure" and urged the Senate Human Rights Committee to investigate cases like Rubina Chandio's murder. Dr Tariq Fazal Chaudhry, Federal Minister for Parliamentary Affairs, assured support for parliamentary committees working on women's rights and pledged government assistance.  Maulana Atta ur Rehman, a JUI-F Senator, also raised concerns about insecurity in Khyber Pakhtunkhwa, citing the targeted killing of Maulana Muhammad Idrees and alleged administrative obstruction of protests.

articles.title: A.P. police registered 19,952 cases of crime against women in 2024, says NCRB report - The Hindu
articles.rephrased_article: Andhra Pradesh police registered 19,952 cases of crime against women in 2024, a decrease from the previous years.  The National Crime Records Bureau (NCRB) reported that 17,149 individuals were arrested for these crimes and chargesheets were filed in 94.4% of the cases. The report highlighted various types of offenses, including harassment by husbands or relatives, sexual harassment, rape, attempted rape, stalking, kidnapping, assault, and murder.  A significant number of kidnapping cases remain pending with 865 cases unresolved at the end of 2024.

articles.title: UK’s ‘first gay dad’ Barrie Drewitt-Barlow and husband charged with rape, sex trafficking | World News - The Times of India
articles.rephrased_article: Barrie Drewitt-Barlow and his husband Scott Hutchison have been charged with multiple serious sexual offences, including rape, sexual assault, and modern slavery trafficking for sexual exploitation. The charges follow police raids at properties in Danbury, Maldon, and Braintree, which were part of an investigation led by Essex Police.  The pair are due to appear before Chelmsford Magistrates’ Court on Friday.

articles.title: Rebel Wilson accused of 'complete revision of history' in Australia defamation case
articles.rephrased_article: Rebel Wilson is facing a defamation lawsuit from young Australian actress Charlotte MacInnes, who alleges that Wilson's Instagram posts harmed her reputation. The case centers on an incident in September 2023 where MacInnes shared a bath with producer Amanda Ghost, which Wilson claims led to a complaint of sexual harassment by MacInnes.  Wilson denies these accusations, and her lawyer argues that MacInnes's career has flourished since the incident. The court is expected to rule on damages for MacInnes.

articles.title: Palestinians expose torture and sexual violence in Israeli detention | Sexual Assault News | Al Jazeera
articles.rephrased_article: Palestinians who were detained in Israeli prisons have shared disturbing accounts of torture, sexual violence, and physical abuse.  Former detainees, including Mohammed al-Bakri and Ahmed, described being stripped naked, subjected to sexual assault by soldiers, and enduring degrading treatment. The Euro-Med Human Rights Monitor documented these cases as part of a broader pattern of systematic abuse within Israeli detention facilities. Kifaya Khraim, from the Women’s Centre for Legal Aid and Counselling, confirmed that allegations of torture and sexual violence are widespread among Palestinian detainees.

articles.title: Superdry co-founder James Holder jailed for rape
articles.rephrased_article: James Holder, co-founder of the fashion company Superdry, was sentenced to eight years in prison for raping a woman in 2022. The victim's statement described the attack as a "living nightmare" and said it continues to impact her life.  Recorder David Chidgey stated that Holder's actions were fueled by entitlement and disregard for the victim's bodily autonomy. Superdry has confirmed Holder resigned from his roles with the company in 2016, and consultancy work ended in 2019. Gloucestershire Police commended the victim for her bravery and resilience.

articles.title: Chirayu Rana hires lawyer who represented Epstein accusers in lawsuit against JPMorgan executive Lorna Hajdini - The Times of India
articles.rephrased_article: Chirayu Rana, a former JPMorgan banker, has hired high-profile lawyer Daniel Kaiser to represent him in a lawsuit against his former supervisor, Lorna Hajdini.  Rana alleges that Hajdini drugged and sexually assaulted him, but JPMorgan denies the claims. The bank conducted an internal investigation which found no evidence supporting Rana's allegations, while Kaiser insists there is more evidence to be presented.

articles.title: Neymar apologises to Robinho’s son after slapping him in training | World Cup 2026 | Al Jazeera
articles.rephrased_article: Neymar publicly apologized to Robinho Jr, the son of former Real Madrid and Manchester City striker Robinho, after slapping him during a training session. The incident occurred on Sunday, prompting an investigation by Santos.  Robinho Jr. confirmed that the situation was resolved and accepted Neymar's apology. Despite the incident, Neymar remains hopeful of being called up for the World Cup later this year.

articles.title: Doctors Without Borders says Israel has 'manufactured malnutrition crisis' in Gaza - World - DAWN.COM
articles.rephrased_article: Doctors Without Borders (MSF) has accused Israel of creating a "manufactured malnutrition crisis" in Gaza, citing data from its analysis of health facilities and the impact of the Israeli blockade. The charity's report found that infants born to malnourished mothers are more likely to be premature and have low birth weight, while 90% of babies born to such mothers were also premature.  MSF also highlighted the impact of the Gaza Humanitarian Foundation (GHF), a US- and Israeli-backed organization, which they say reduced food distribution points in Gaza and led to violence and malnutrition. The charity called for immediate unhindered access to aid into Gaza.

articles.title: Woman jailed in Somalia for peaceful protest ‘stripped, kicked and beaten’ | Global development | The Guardian
articles.rephrased_article: Sadia Moalim Ali, a 27-year-old Somali nursing graduate and activist, has been detained in prison for her anti-government activism. She claims to have been tortured by guards while being held in solitary confinement without food or basic necessities.  Ali was arrested on April 12th for criticizing the government's policies on social media. Amnesty International reports that police are holding her without due legal process and she has not been formally charged. Human rights organizations, including Dalmar Dhayow of the Coalition of Somali Human Rights Defenders, have condemned Ali's detention as unlawful and called for her immediate release.

articles.title: Neo-Nazi Joel Davis charged with inciting hatred over ‘Abolish the Jewish lobby’ rally at NSW parliament | New South Wales | The Guardian
articles.rephrased_article: Joel Davis, a prominent neo-Nazi, has been charged with alleged hate speech after a protest by the National Socialist Network outside New South Wales parliament last year.  Police investigated the event and two speeches allegedly made by participants, leading to his arrest at a South Penrith house. The charge stems from an incident where a banner reading "Abolish the Jewish lobby" was displayed. Davis is facing charges of publicly inciting hatred on grounds of race and causing fear. He has been granted conditional bail and will appear in court on June 3rd.

articles.title: Congress leader Varsha Gaikwad writes to Maharashtra Governor, seeks immediate enactment of Shakti Bill - The Hindu
articles.rephrased_article: Varsha Gaikwad, Mumbai Congress president and MP, has written to Maharashtra Governor Jishnu Dev Varma urging urgent action on rising crimes against women in the state.  Gaikwad requested the Governor's intervention regarding the Shakti Criminal Laws (Maharashtra Amendment) Bill, 2020, which awaits presidential assent, and urged the government to take strict action against atrocities against women. The letter comes amid protests following a four-year-old girl's alleged rape and murder in Pune district.

articles.title: 65% of newly elected Bengal MLAs face criminal cases; 61% are ‘crorepatis’: ADR - The Hindu
articles.rephrased_article: The Association for Democratic Reforms (ADR) reported that 65% of newly elected legislators in the West Bengal Assembly have declared criminal cases, a significant increase from previous elections.  Of these, 58% face serious charges, including murder and attempt to murder. The report also found that 74% of winning candidates from the Bharatiya Janata Party and 43% from the All India Trinamool Congress have declared criminal cases.  The total assets of all winning candidates stand at ₹1,091 crore, with an average asset of Rs 3.73 crore per MLA. The report also highlighted concerns about the rising wealth among elected representatives and under-representation of women in the legislature.

articles.title: Venice Biennale faces backlash after including Russia
articles.rephrased_article: The 61st Venice Biennale is facing backlash over Russia's reinstatement, with activists protesting the inclusion of the nation and its pavilion.  Pussy Riot, Femen, and other groups have staged demonstrations outside the Russian national pavilion, criticizing Russia's war in Ukraine and accusing it of using the event as a platform for cultural dominance. The European Commission has threatened to withhold funding, while Italy's culture minister will not attend the opening. Despite the controversy, Russia maintains its presence at the Biennale, with the pavilion featuring experimental sound performances and an upside-down tree. Ukrainian artists like Zhanna Kadyrova are also exhibiting their work, highlighting the impact of the war on their country.

articles.title: 'Don't let him die': Teacher accused of murdering baby begged medics to save son, UK court hears - The Times of India
articles.rephrased_article: Jamie Varley, a 37-year-old teacher, is facing charges of murder, sexual assault, and child cruelty in connection with the death of his 13-month-old adopted son, Preston. Preston Davey was found unconscious at Blackpool Victoria Hospital on Tuesday after suffering severe mistreatment during his time with Varley and his companion, John McGowan-Fazakerley. Medical professionals testified that Preston showed no signs of water inhalation in his lungs, contradicting Varley's account of leaving the child alone in a bath. The prosecution alleges that Varley abused the child physically and sexually, while McGowan-Fazakerley also faces charges related to child cruelty and sexual assault.  The case has garnered significant public attention due to its serious nature and the potential implications for adoptive care arrangements.

articles.title: JPMorgan offered $1 million, Chirayu Rana demanded $20 million in sexual harassment lawsuit against Lorna Hajdini: Report - The Times of India
articles.rephrased_article: JPMorgan Chase is facing a legal battle with former banker Chirayu Rana, who has accused senior executive Lorna Hajdini of sexual abuse.  Rana allegedly demanded $20 million from the bank before filing his lawsuit, which alleges drugging, forced sexual encounters, and racist abuse. The bank offered him $1 million to settle but he counter-offered $11.75 million. While JPMorgan maintains there is no evidence of wrongdoing, Rana's lawyer claims the allegations will be supported by evidence as the case progresses.

articles.title: Ex-Scottish council leader Jordan Linden jailed for 18 months over sex crimes against boys, young men - The Times of India
articles.rephrased_article: Jordan Linden, a former Scottish National Party (SNP) council leader, was sentenced to 18 months in prison for multiple sexual offenses against boys and young men.  Linden was convicted of ten offences including sexual assault, stalking, and inappropriate sexual communication after a trial earlier this year. The court rejected a plea for leniency from Linden's defense lawyer, citing his difficult teenage years and autism diagnosis. David Moggach KC, Linden's lawyer, argued that the offenses were not as serious as they appeared.  The case has sparked political controversy with questions raised over how prior complaints were handled within the party and youth organizations.

articles.title: Indian national accused of laundering $7 million from illegal tobacco trade, submitting fraudulent residency papers in Australia - The Times of India
articles.rephrased_article: An Indian national, 33 years old, is facing multiple charges in Brisbane, Australia for allegedly laundering over $7 million linked to an illegal tobacco network and providing false information to immigration authorities. The Australian Federal Police (AFP) conducted a search warrant operation on April 27th at a Kuraby property with support from the Australian Border Force (ABF) and Queensland Police Service (QPS), seizing cash, mobile phones, business records, and vaping products.  The man is scheduled to appear in court on June 26th, 2026.

articles.title: ‘She invited me to bedroom and...’: Fresh claims emerge in JPMorgan sex harassment case involving Chirayu Rana and Lorna Hajdini - The Times of India
articles.rephrased_article: Lorna Hajdini, a senior executive at JPMorgan, is facing allegations of sexual harassment from former banker Chirayu Rana. Two unnamed witnesses have provided sworn statements corroborating Rana's claims, detailing incidents involving alleged coercion and inappropriate behavior by Hajdini.  Rana alleges that Hajdini drugged him with Viagra and forced him into non-consensual sex acts over several months. JPMorgan has denied all accusations and stated there is no evidence to support them, while Rana’s lawyer insists the case is genuine.

articles.title: US cancels visas for board of Costa Rica newspaper critical of Trump ally | Costa Rica | The Guardian
articles.rephrased_article: The US State Department has revoked tourist visas for over half of the board members of La Nación, Costa Rica's leading national newspaper, which has been critical of President Rodrigo Chaves.  This action follows a pattern of visa restrictions targeting Costa Rican individuals who are political opponents or critics of the government. The move is seen as an attack on press freedom and political discussion in Costa Rica by analysts. The US State Department did not immediately respond to requests for comment.

articles.title: India, Vietnam elevate ties to enhanced comprehensive strategic partnership; set $25 billion trade target - The Hindu
articles.rephrased_article: Prime Minister Narendra Modi and Vietnamese President To Lam elevated their bilateral ties to an enhanced comprehensive strategic partnership, setting a $25 billion annual trade target by 2030. The two leaders signed 13 agreements covering areas such as digital payments, rare earth minerals, pharmaceuticals, education, banking, and culture.  They also discussed the Indo-Pacific region amid China's growing assertiveness in the South China Sea, agreeing to continue contributing to peace, stability, and prosperity. Modi highlighted India's gratitude for Vietnam's condemnation of the Pahalgam terrorist attack and its support in combating terrorism.

articles.title: IS families in Syria have booked tickets home to Australia, minister says
articles.rephrased_article: Australian Home Affairs Minister Tony Burke announced that 13 women and children with links to Islamic State (IS) have booked tickets home to Australia. The group, which includes wives, widows, and children of IS fighters, will be met by authorities upon arrival who plan to arrest those suspected of committing crimes.  The Australian Federal Police (AFP) Commissioner Krissy Barrett stated that the government has been preparing for their return since 2014 and will investigate all members of the group. The children will receive community integration programs while the adults face potential legal action.

articles.title: Mamata Banerjee, West Bengal election results 2026: India’s fiercest female politician faces a fight for survival
articles.rephrased_article: Mamata Banerjee, the fierce leader of India's Trinamool Congress (TMC) party, suffered a defeat in the West Bengal state elections, ending her bid for a fourth consecutive term as chief minister.  Her loss marks a significant shift in the political landscape of the region and raises questions about her future. The victory of the Bharatiya Janata Party (BJP) signals a potential power shift and could lead to internal divisions within the TMC. Banerjee's legacy, built on street protests and a commitment to the common man, is now facing uncertainty as she navigates this new political reality.

articles.title: Andrew Tate sought CPS assurance he would not be arrested if he returned to UK, court hears | UK news | The Guardian
articles.rephrased_article: Andrew Tate and his brother Tristan Tate sought written assurances from the Crown Prosecution Service (CPS) that they wouldn't be arrested if they returned to the UK for a civil case. The CPS declined, stating there was no reason to withdraw warrants, and that they could not provide assurances of non-arrest.  The Tates are facing 21 criminal charges in the UK and 10 charges in Romania, with both brothers denying all wrongdoing. A judge will decide on a stay for the civil case and delay the trial date.

articles.title: What’s happening in Mali one week after attack by armed groups? All we know | Armed Groups News | Al Jazeera
articles.rephrased_article: Assimi Goita, the leader of Mali’s military government, has assumed the role of defense minister following the death of his predecessor.  The attacks by armed groups, including al-Qaeda-linked JNIM and the Tuareg-dominated FLA, have resulted in a security crisis, with at least 23 people killed and civilians facing hunger and potential harm. The situation is further complicated by Russian mercenary group Wagner's presence in Mali, which has been accused of protecting the military government while also clashing with JNIM fighters.
