The UN Human Rights Office has called for an end to the fighting and protection of civilians.

articles.title: 'I own you, Brownie': Ex-JPMorgan banker Chirayu Rana brings 'threesome' allegation against Lorna Hajdini - The Times of India
articles.rephrased_article: Chirayu Rana, a former JPMorgan banker, has filed a new lawsuit against Lorna Hajdini, alleging sexual assault. The lawsuit includes witness statements from an anonymous friend who claims to have witnessed Hajdini's behavior, including waking him up naked and pressuring him into sexual encounters.  The new filing follows JPMorgan's denial of the allegations and claim that Rana never reported them.

articles.title: Bayern Munich vs PSG: Champions League – preview, team news, start, lineups | Football News | Al Jazeera
articles.rephrased_article: Bayern Munich and Paris Saint-Germain face off in the Champions League semifinal second leg on Wednesday.  The French team holds a 5-4 lead after an incredible first leg, with both coaches promising more attacking football. Bayern Munich, seeking their sixth European Cup title, will rely on their high-scoring offense, while PSG aims to secure its place in the final against either Arsenal or Atletico Madrid.  The match is set for a 9pm (19:00 GMT) kickoff at the Allianz Arena.

articles.title: Pune child rape-murder: Postmortem report points to asphyxia as cause of death, says police - The Hindu
articles.rephrased_article: Police in Pune have determined that a four-year-old girl's death was caused by asphyxia, likely resulting from being gagged with a cloth. The 65-year-old accused, who has a history of molestation charges, is currently under arrest and faces accusations of sexual assault and murder.

articles.title: Alan Jones claims invalid warrants, police impropriety and ‘willy-nilly’ search in sex abuse investigation | Alan Jones | The Guardian
articles.rephrased_article: Alan Jones, a former Australian radio shock jock, is facing 25 charges of indecent assault and two charges of sexual touching against nine alleged victims. Police conducted a search of his Sydney home in November 2024 as part of an eight-month investigation into historical sexual abuse allegations.  Jones's lawyers claim the search warrants were invalid because they referred to offenses not included in the eventual charges, and that officers may have searched his phone without proper authorization. The NSW police commissioner is defending the search warrant and its legality. Jones will contest the allegations in a four-month trial beginning in August.

articles.title: Nasrapur rape and murder | Child rights body seeks special prosecutor, fast-tracking of the case - The Hindu
articles.rephrased_article: The Maharashtra State Commission for Protection of Child Rights urged the state government to appoint a special public prosecutor and move the Nasrapur rape and murder case to a fast-track court. The case involves an alleged rape and murder of a four-year-old girl in Pune's Bhor taluka on May 1st, prompting protests and disruptions in the region.

articles.title: Canadian fiddler sues Google after AI Overview wrongly claimed he was a sex offender | Music | The Guardian
articles.rephrased_article: Ashley MacIsaac, a three-time Juno award-winning musician, filed a $1.5 million civil lawsuit against Google in the Ontario superior court of justice, alleging defamation by its AI-generated Overview feature. The lawsuit claims that Google's AI falsely identified MacIsaac as a sex offender and wrongly stated he was listed on the national sex offender registry.  MacIsaac is seeking damages for injuries and losses resulting from the inaccurate information published by the AI.

articles.title: Blake Lively and Justin Baldoni settle lawsuit over acrimonious It Ends With Us production | Blake Lively | The Guardian
articles.rephrased_article: Blake Lively and Justin Baldoni have reached a settlement in their legal dispute over the production of their film "It Ends With Us."  The joint statement expressed pride in the finished product and stated commitment to creating respectful work environments. The settlement details were not disclosed, but both parties acknowledged challenges during production and agreed to move forward constructively.

articles.title: LHC suspends defamation case verdict against Meesha Shafi to the extent of payment of damages - Pakistan - DAWN.COM
articles.rephrased_article: The Lahore High Court partially suspended a lower court's order requiring singer-actor Ali Zafar to receive Rs5 million in damages from Meesha Shafi for defamation. The court allowed Shafi to deposit half the amount and provide a surety bond for the remaining sum, while maintaining her restriction on repeating allegations of sexual harassment against Zafar. The decision came after Shafi appealed the lower court's ruling.  The case is ongoing with both parties receiving notices from the court.
